key_idea: Build the hull of the controlled trees once; for each outside candidate the hull edges it sees form one contiguous arc, so find the two tangent vertices by binary search and get the new area from prefix sums of cross products along the remaining chain plus the two edges through the new point.
sketch: Compute the CCW hull of the first k points (monotone chain) and prefix sums pre[i] of cross(h[j], h[j+1]). For a candidate P, an edge is visible iff cross(h[i], h[i+1], P) < 0. To seed the search, locate one visible and one invisible edge in O(log m): if P.x is strictly inside the hull's x-range, binary search the lower-chain and upper-chain edges spanning P.x (neither visible means P is inside, skip); otherwise one of the two edges at the extreme vertex on P's side is visible and one of the two edges at the opposite extreme vertex is invisible. Two binary searches along the cyclic arcs between those edges give the first and last visible edges; the new doubled area is the chain sum from the end of the last visible edge to the start of the first visible edge plus cross(h[a], P) + cross(P, h[s]). Take the maximum, O((n + k) log k) overall. Pitfalls: prefix cross sums about the origin overflow 64 bits, so use __int128 (the final doubled area is at most 8e18); print exactly one decimal from the integer doubled area (.0 or .5) rather than through floating point; candidates inside the hull leave the area unchanged. Verified against an O(n * hull) brute force on 1500 random cases.
